findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced 10x without justification
findings.body: In pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 the ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The PR description does not mention this and it is unrelated to the deadlock fix. Consequence: all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) now run 10x as often, increasing DB load 10x and making overlapping runs likely since the job has a 9 minute timeout but fires every minute. Should be reverted.

findings.title: Routine cleanup progress logged at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579 routine progress ("Annotations to clean by time/count", "cleaned annotations", "Tags to clean") is logged with r.log.Error, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs), cond, and a nil err. Consequence: every cleanup cycle emits Error-level logs with up to hundreds of KB per batch, flooding error logs, triggering false alerts, hiding real errors, and adding CPU/IO cost. Should be Debug and should not log every ID.

findings.title: Split SELECT OFFSET + DELETE can delete annotations that should be retained
findings.body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go CleanAnnotations MaxCount path (around line 549) the code first does SELECT id FROM annotation WHERE <type> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT batch OFFSET MaxCount in one session, then DELETE FROM annotation WHERE id IN (...) in a separate session. The old single-statement DELETE with subquery was atomic. With concurrent inserts between SELECT and DELETE the ranking shifts: IDs that were beyond MaxCount at SELECT time can be within the newest MaxCount that must be kept at DELETE time, yet they are still deleted. Consequence: recently created annotations that should be retained are incorrectly deleted (data loss). MaxAge path is stable on cutoff time, but MaxCount path is order-unstable.

findings.title: Batched loop stops on zero rows affected instead of empty fetch
findings.body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go untilDoneOrCancelled line 656 stops when affected==0, where affected is RowsAffected from DELETE. If fetchIDs returns N IDs but the subsequent DELETE affects 0 rows due to a concurrent deleter racing the same IDs, the loop exits even though many rows beyond the first LIMIT batch remain unvisited. The correct termination is empty fetch, not zero affected. Consequence: incomplete cleanup that needs extra cycles to drain, and starvation under contention.

findings.title: SQLite ID list built with quadratic string concatenation
findings.body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go line 611 the SQLite fallback builds the IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. This copies the growing string each iteration, O(n^2). With batch sizes like 32767 exercised in tests this copies hundreds of MB. Consequence: CPU and latency spike during cleanup. Should use strings.Builder.
